messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] NAT gateway health checks failing for nat-0a1b2c3d4e in us-east-1-az2. 5xx spike on private subnet calls. Paging eng-oncall and infra.

maya (SRE): paging received, looking.

simon (infra): seeing ICMP/tracepack hang to 10.2.1.1 (NAT ENI). health-checks show timeouts.

lisa (prodops): i pushed a NACL tighten to block ephemeral range 32768-61000 in az2 ~T-12m for a different hardening ticket. reverting if that's the culprit.

maya (SRE): copy. ram, any customer impact notes / numbers?

ram (support): yes — embeddings & generation endpoints. Status page draft ready. ~14 customer reports so far. spike started ~T-15m.

simon (infra): quick triage: route table rtb-0f1e2d3c points 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-0a1b2c3d4e (degraded). provider console shows nat health flapping. attempting quick reroute to healthy nat in same AZ.

maya (SRE): go ahead but keep things reversible. also rollback the NACL change; that could amplify TCP ephemeral failures.

simon (infra): running replacement:
```bash
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0f1e2d3c --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0fdecaf --region us-east-1
```

simon (infra): route replaced, checking connectivity.

lisa (prodops): rolling back NACL entry now:
```bash
aws ec2 replace-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-12345678 --rule-number 100 --protocol -1 --egress --rule-action allow --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --region us-east-1
```

lisa (prodops): rollback applied.

maya (SRE): traffic metrics: error rate dropping from ~30% -> ~6% in last 6m. keep monitoring.

oncall-bot: [INCIDENT CREATED] INC-2026-4312 | priority: P0 | channels: #incidents #eng-oncall #prodops | creator: oncall-bot

simon (infra): provider status: NAT instance nat-0a1b2c3d4e shows upstream AZ fabric errors; provider attempted internal failover but health checks remained failing. our route was still targeted at the degraded nat until replacement.

ram (support): updated status page and sent customer-notify. message: transient connectivity errors for some customers in us-east-1 az2, services recovering.

maya (SRE): mitigation summary: - replaced route to healthy nat - rolled back NACL tighten - results: errors dropped, service recovered.

lisa (prodops): thumbs up. copying timeline to the incident doc.

simon (infra): opening provider ticket now for RCA and whether nat-0a1b2c3d4e should be drained/decommed. ticket #PROV-789432.

maya (SRE): capturing follow-ups for postmortem: 1) avoid manual NACL tighten during active deploy window, 2) add a short canary and wait-for-metrics before infra-wide NACL changes, 3) automate route failover to warm-standby NAT when provider health < 0.8.

eng-oncall: taking next-oncall shift at 12:30 UTC, will monitor post-mitigation for 2 hours.

maya (SRE): saving logs and dashboards -> /var/log/incidents/1768539999.log and pinned dashboard on console. starting postmortem doc.

ram (support): i’ll follow up with affected customer threads, mark impacted accounts, and close incident page after provider confirmation.

oncall-bot: incident state updated to: mitigated -> monitoring (updated by maya).

simon (infra): follow-up suggestion: add pre-check in routing automation to refuse replacing route to a NAT resource flagged by the provider API as degraded.

maya (SRE): agreed. handing off to simon for provider liaison and eng-oncall for follow-ups. handoff notes attached in the incident doc.

eng-oncall: handoff acknowledged. ongoing monitoring for 2h. will escalate if error rate ticks up. :thumbsup:

maya (SRE): final quick summary for handoff: customer impact ~15-20m of elevated errors for some endpoints. root cause likely combo of provider NAT flapping + our NACL change. action items: postmortem, provider RCA, add canary + automation checks.

simon (infra): ack. leaving provider ticket open. will report back when it's resolved.

ram (support): thanks team — good fast mitigation.
